\section[la sinceridad]{la sinceridad — sincerity, frankness}

\label{lesson:ES-C724-sinceridad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for stingy, then the Spanish for cruel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la sinceridad}
\textbf{la sinceridad} — \textquotedblleft{}sincerity, frankness\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Te lo digo con toda sinceridad.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I am telling you in all honesty.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Con sinceridad} — honestly, frankly.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sinceridad} is usually described as a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{sinceritās} \textquotedblleft{}purity, soundness\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{sincērus} \textquotedblleft{}genuine\textquotedblright{}, the source of \emph{sincero} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la sinceridad}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la sinceridad}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la sinceridad}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for stingy, then the Spanish for cruel, then say \emph{la sinceridad} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does la sinceridad mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Sincerity, frankness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[cotillear]{cotillear — to gossip}

\label{lesson:ES-C724-cotillear}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for cruel, then the Spanish for sincerity.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: cotillear}
\textbf{cotillear} — \textquotedblleft{}to gossip\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Mis vecinas cotillean en la escalera.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My neighbours gossip on the stairs.}
\end{quote}

Spain; a gossip is \emph{un cotilla}. In Latin America people say \emph{chismear}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{cotillear} is built on \emph{cotilla} \textquotedblleft{}a gossip\textquotedblright{} with the ending \emph{-ear}. For \emph{cotilla} in this sense the origin is not settled; an older \emph{cotilla} was a corset.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cotillear}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cotillear}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{cotillear}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for cruel, then the Spanish for sincerity, then say \emph{cotillear} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does cotillear mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To gossip\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[mentiroso]{mentiroso — lying; the liar}

\label{lesson:ES-C724-mentiroso}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for sincerity, then the Spanish for to gossip.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: mentiroso}
\textbf{mentiroso} — \textquotedblleft{}lying; the liar\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Eres un mentiroso.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{You are a liar.}
\end{quote}

Feminine \emph{mentirosa}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mentiroso} is built on \emph{mentira} \textquotedblleft{}lie\textquotedblright{} with the ending \emph{-oso}; \emph{mentir} comes from Latin \emph{mentīrī} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[sincero]{sincero — sincere, honest}

\label{lesson:ES-C724-sincero}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to gossip, then the Spanish for lying.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: sincero}
\textbf{sincero} — \textquotedblleft{}sincere, honest\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Para ser sincero, no me gusta.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{To be honest, I do not like it.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Para ser sincero} — to be honest.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sincero} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{sincērus} \textquotedblleft{}pure, genuine\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[la honestidad]{la honestidad — honesty}

\label{lesson:ES-C724-honestidad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for lying, then the Spanish for sincere.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la honestidad}
\textbf{la honestidad} — \textquotedblleft{}honesty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Valoro la honestidad de mis amigos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{I value my friends' honesty.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Honradez} is a close synonym.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{honestidad} is built on \emph{honesto}, which comes from Latin \emph{honestus} \textquotedblleft{}honourable\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), itself built on \emph{honōs} \textquotedblleft{}honour\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{la honestidad}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{la honestidad}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for lying, then the Spanish for sincere, then say \emph{la honestidad} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
